title: Vaughn E. Hathaway, Jr., et al. v. Grace Presbytery
disposition_detail: The Judicial Commission did not sustain any of the complainant's four specifications (14–0) and upheld Grace Presbytery's decision (14–0).
first_summary: Vaughn Hathaway and others complained that Grace Presbytery improperly approved and proceeded to ordain and install a candidate who had been divorced for his adultery and had remarried, contrary to Scripture, the Westminster Confession, BCO 16-3, and the Seventh General Assembly divorce report. The Judicial Commission declined to sustain the complaint, reasoning that the PCA has no explicit constitutional statement on divorce and remarriage for officers.
summary: A complaint challenged Grace Presbytery's approval and installation of a candidate who had been divorced for his own infidelity and had remarried; the complainants argued Scripture, the Westminster Confession, BCO 16-3, and the Seventh General Assembly's divorce report barred ordination. The Judicial Commission did not sustain any of the four specifications and upheld Presbytery's action. Its adopted reason was that the PCA's constitutional statements do not explicitly address divorce and remarriage for church officers; noting wide interpretive disagreement, it called for study. The ordination and installation remained undisturbed.

evidence_notes.identity_and_adoption: Case #2, TE Vaughn E. Hathaway, Jr., et al. v. Grace Presbytery, 14th General Assembly (1986), decided by the Committee on Judicial Business/Judicial Commission. The adjudication is headed 'ADJUDICATION OF CASE 2' and the judgment ends 'Adopted' at cases/ga14_1986__case2.md (sha256 acd15c0f1839085699c4d73f078ad701b7c63c1235ae26f5d5cf17f373a30852), lines 47–77; printed pp. 150–151. Commission roster at lines 79–83.
evidence_notes.dispute: Complainants challenged Grace Presbytery's August 30, 1985 approval of a candidate's ordination trials and vote to proceed to ordination and installation after he disclosed that his former spouse had divorced him for his infidelity and that he had remarried; grounds were Scripture, Westminster Confession XXIV.5, BCO 16-3, and the 7th General Assembly divorce report. See lines 13–37; Presbytery denied the complaint October 8, 1985, lines 45 and 55; the candidate was ordained and installed September 15, 1985, line 57.
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: The Commission voted not to sustain the complaint on each point (lines 71–77), and the minutes record that each specification one through four was not sustained 14–0 and the lower court's decision was upheld 14–0 (lines 103–106). The adopted reason was that there is no explicit PCA constitutional statement on divorce and remarriage, particularly for church officers; the Commission acknowledged wide disagreement over biblical interpretation and urged study (lines 73–77).
evidence_notes.qualifications: The candidate and church names are withheld to protect privacy (line 43); the respondent objected to Items 1-A and 4-C,D (line 91); the complaint was first filed with and denied by Presbytery before being submitted to the General Assembly (lines 45, 55, and 59). No separate concurrence or dissent appears in the supplied record, and the Commission did not remand or impose discipline.
evidence_notes.incorporated_decisions: No separate judicial decision is incorporated by reference. The Commission upheld the lower court's action (lines 105–106), but the lower court's denial is reported only as the underlying action and is not supplied as a separate opinion; its result is sufficiently stated at lines 45 and 55.

source_limits: The supplied record includes the complaint, the Commission's adjudication, and the Commission minutes, but not a verbatim transcript or a separate Presbytery opinion; the Presbytery's denial was on the merits without debate. Candidate and church names are withheld in the source.
